claims.text: Bass X Machina premieres globally on Netflix on November 3, 2026.

Bass X Machina premieres on Netflix on November 3, 2026. Netflix's official media center lists that date for the United States, while its broader animation announcement presents the series as part of the platform's global animated slate.
Bass X Machina is a Netflix series. Availability is tied to Netflix's regional catalogs, so AniNextUp will keep the release guide updated if the service publishes territory-specific differences.

The story takes place in a lawless steampunk West populated by violent outlaws, machines and supernatural threats. A father is forced into the roles of judge, jury and executioner while trying to protect his family, even as every violent decision risks pushing those same people away.

LeSean Thomas created the series and Studio Mir handles animation. Brian Tyree Henry stars and is also an executive producer alongside Thomas, Jennifer Wiley-Moxley and Chad Handley. The cast also includes Tati Gabrielle and Cree Summer.

Dreamland starts streaming on Crunchyroll on October 16, 2026. Its Japanese television broadcast begins October 17 in the ANiMAZiNG!!! block on ABC TV and the TV Asahi network, scheduled for 2:00 a.m. JST. The one-day difference is therefore intentional: the international streaming date and Japanese TV date are not the same.

Crunchyroll lists the series for North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East and CIS. Availability can still vary within individual catalogs, so viewers should check their local service listing.

Terrence has lived with a fear of fire since losing his mother. When he finally confronts that fear inside his nightmares, he becomes a Traveler—someone capable of exploring Dreamland, a world created from humanity's dreams and nightmares.

Dreamland adapts the French comic by Reno Lemaire. Juan Pablo Machado directs at Ellipse Animation and La Chouette Compagnie, with series composition credited to Jean-Luc Cano and Antoine Maurel. The Japanese version features a localized voice cast for its domestic broadcast.
The Japanese-version promotional campaign also confirmed Faulieu. for the opening theme “movin'on” and Ai Tomioka for the ending theme “dream catcher.”
DARK MACHINE THE ANIMATION premieres October 13, 2026 on Fuji TV in Japan and streams internationally on Crunchyroll. The exact Crunchyroll release time is still TBA.

DARK MACHINE THE ANIMATION premieres October 13, 2026. Fuji TV lists the first broadcast for Tuesday at 25:45 JST, which is 1:45 a.m. JST on October 14 in standard clock notation. Kansai TV follows on October 15 at 26:45 JST, while BS Fuji begins October 20 at 24:30 JST. Broadcast times may change.

Crunchyroll lists October 13 for the subtitled simulcast, but its Fall 2026 schedule currently shows the airtime as TBA. AniNextUp will add the international release time when Crunchyroll publishes it rather than converting the Japanese TV time into an unconfirmed global time.

Crunchyroll has confirmed the anime for North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, CIS and India. In Japan, unlimited streaming begins progressively on October 14 at 12:00 JST on d Anime Store, Hulu, Lemino, DMM TV, FOD, Bandai Channel, U-NEXT, Anime Hodai, Amazon Prime Video, Anime Times, TELASA, J:COM STREAM, milplus and ABEMA Premium. Free latest-episode distribution is also scheduled through ABEMA, TVer and Niconico.
Kairi arrives in Golden Valley searching for the legendary Senki and is pulled into the competitive world of DARK MACHINE after meeting Rudra.

Cour 2 begins October 13, 2026. The official schedule lists AT-X on Tuesdays at 11:00 p.m. JST, while TOKYO MX, BS11, Sun TV and KBS Kyoto air it at 24:30. Other Japanese stations follow at later times.
Yes. The official site confirms that episode 13.5, a recap of the story so far, airs during the week before the Cour 2 premiere. The regular second-cour story then resumes on October 13.

Japanese streaming includes ABEMA and d Anime Store among the earliest services, followed by Prime Video, U-NEXT, Hulu and other platforms on later schedules. Crunchyroll carries the series internationally in supported territories; exact release timing can vary by region.
The second cour continues the Asuka storyline and moves into material centered on Haru Aomi, a member of the girls' basketball club. The second Cour 2 PV previews both parts of the continuing story.
HORROR COLLECTOR premieres October 10, 2026. The Japanese television broadcast begins on NHK General TV, bringing the children's horror novel series to television animation.
HORROR COLLECTOR is included in Crunchyroll's Fall 2026 international lineup. Streaming availability and exact episode timing can vary by territory, while the Japanese broadcast is handled by NHK.
The first television season is confirmed for 12 episodes. That gives the adaptation a defined single-cour run for its first collection of supernatural stories.

Fushigi, a mysterious boy in a red hood, travels from place to place collecting urban legends that have taken physical form. He pursues Himitsu alongside his unusual partner Jimmy as the series explores frightening rumors and phenomena that may be much closer to everyday life than they first appear.

Japanese singer-songwriter Shikao Suga wrote and performs both the opening and ending themes. The official announcement notes his own interest in J-horror and describes the anime as a fusion of urban legends and Japanese horror.
Studio Palette handles the animation production. AniNextUp will continue tracking the weekly schedule and any regional streaming updates after the October 10 premiere.
A Certain Dark Item begins its Japanese television run on October 9, 2026. Here are the confirmed broadcast details, streaming guidance, story and official trailer.

A Certain Dark Item begins broadcasting in Japan on October 9, 2026. AT-X lists 10:30 p.m. JST on October 9; Tokyo MX and BS11 list 12:30 a.m. JST on October 10 (shown as October 9 at 24:30 in Japanese schedules). These are Japan broadcast times, not worldwide streaming times. See the official broadcast schedule.

Crunchyroll lists the anime in its Fall 2026 international lineup. Availability and episode release times vary by region, so viewers should consult their local Crunchyroll catalog. Japan's television and streaming services follow their own schedules, which do not establish availability outside Japan.

The series follows ITEM, an elite four-girl team carrying out covert missions in Academy City's criminal underworld. Its members are Shizuri Mugino, Rikou Takitsubo, Frenda Seivelun and Saiai Kinuhata. The official introduction describes the arrival of a mysterious fifth girl, whose encounter with ITEM pulls the group into a deeper conflict. The official episode-one synopsis introduces a mission against an organization conducting inhumane ability-development research under the guise of medical treatment.

J.C.STAFF produces the anime, with Tatsuyuki Nagai directing, Shogo Yasukawa handling series composition and Shigeki Kimoto designing the characters. The official staff and cast page confirms Ami Koshimizu as Shizuri Mugino, Aya Suzaki as Rikou Takitsubo, Maaya Uchida as Frenda Seivelun, Chinatsu Akasaki as Saiai Kinuhata and Hana Hishikawa as Choubi Kano. East Of Eden performs the opening theme “Ghost Sequence,” while Kishida Kyoudan & The Akeboshi Rockets performs the ending theme “Genshi Kuzushi (Meltdowner).”

The official anime website publishes the latest promotional footage and key visuals. The official main trailer confirms the Japanese premiere and theme music. For updated episode listings, consult the official schedule and official news.
Dandivine premieres in Japan on October 7, 2026. The official Aniplex schedule lists TOKYO MX, BS11, Gunma TV and Tochigi TV at 24:30 JST, with additional broadcasts on Chukyo TV, MBS and AT-X.

In Japan, d Anime Store begins the fastest streaming release alongside the October 7 broadcast, with other services following progressively. Crunchyroll has also included Dandivine in its Fall 2026 international lineup, although availability can differ by territory.

Twenty years after the combining robot Dandivine defeated the mysterious Aposdoll, the world has returned to peace. When the enemy appears again in Tokyo, high school student Gekiha Shijima becomes connected to the legendary machine and a new battle begins.

Dandivine is the first title in the “God of Combined” project, built around the culture of combining robots and developed with merchandise and animation planned together. Aniplex lists LIDENFILMS on the project, with the series positioned as an original mecha production.
The World's Strongest Witch premieres October 7, 2026 on Crunchyroll.

The World's Strongest Witch premieres October 7, 2026. The official Japanese site lists TOKYO MX at 10:00 p.m. JST and BS11 at midnight, with TV Aichi, AT-X and MBS joining on their respective schedules.

ABEMA and d Anime Store begin advance streaming in Japan on October 7 at 10:00 p.m. JST. Crunchyroll also streams the series internationally in a wide group of territories, including North America, Latin America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East and parts of Asia.

Lorna Hermit is cast aside after receiving an ability that appears useless, but her SSS-rank “Internet” skill gives her access to knowledge that changes what she can accomplish. Freed from her former family's plans, she sets out into the wider world and encounters quests that turn that unusual advantage into real power.
The official production credits list Joji Furuta as director, Shoji Yonemura for series composition and Yuki Morimoto for character design. Animation production is handled by Bridge and AISLE.
The Vermilion Mask premieres October 10, 2026 on Crunchyroll.

The Vermilion Mask premieres October 10, 2026 on Crunchyroll. The confirmed simulcast time is 2:30 a.m. PT. In Japan, the anime airs Saturdays at 5:30 p.m. on the Yomiuri TV/Nippon TV nationwide network, excluding some regions.

Crunchyroll lists the anime for North America, Central and South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, CIS and the Indian Subcontinent. Availability can still differ by individual market.

Peru is the pupil of legendary mask maker Gaston Roux. After the Mask of the Warrior God takes control of him and causes a tragedy that kills his friends and master, Peru vows to destroy the remaining masks Gaston created around the world.

Tetsuaki Watanabe directs, with Gai Hazako as assistant director and Daisuke Ohigashi handling series composition. Hisashi Higashijima is character designer and chief animation director, Alisa Okehazama composes the music, and 100studio handles animation production.
